title: Pre-Analysis — Rudder Diverter Strip Standard Against the Repair Scheme Interaction
abstract: Closed work order checking whether the extended diverter strip standard could coexist with the panel repair scheme, raised after a repair station reported that the two sets of instructions did not agree.

sections.objective: Establish whether the extended lightning diverter strip standard and the trailing edge panel repair scheme can both be applied to the same panel, after a repair station reported that a panel carrying a scarf repair could not be brought to the strip standard as written. The work order was raised on a specific aircraft and then widened to the fleet.
sections.findings_summary: The two are compatible but the instructions were not. The repair scheme places its scarf boundary without regard to the diverter strip route, and the strip standard assumes an undamaged laminate under the termination. On the aircraft that raised the question the scarf ran within thirty millimetres of a termination, which the strip standard does not permit and the repair scheme does not prohibit. Nothing is unsafe: the repair is substantiated and the strip is intact. What is missing is a rule about the order in which the two are done and a minimum separation between a repair boundary and a termination. Three documents are involved and all three are silent on it. The bonding resistance measurement task is the one place where the interaction would show up in service, and its acceptance does not distinguish a repaired panel from an intact one.
sections.next_steps: Add a minimum separation between a repair boundary and a diverter strip termination to the repair scheme. State in the strip standard that the panel must be free of repair within that distance. Add a note to the bonding measurement task that a repaired panel is measured against the same limit and is not given an allowance.

similarity_seeds: lightning attachment burn at a trailing edge panel joint
scarf repair boundary near a bonded termination

tasks.title: Establish the geometry on the aircraft that raised the question
Compare the repair scheme boundary rules with the strip route
Check whether the bonding measurement would detect the interaction

evidence.similarity_note: Both entity linking on the panel and doubler part numbers and similarity on the repair vocabulary returned this scheme.

expected_findings.rationale: The repair scheme places its scarf boundary without reference to the diverter strip route, and the strip standard assumes an undamaged laminate under each termination. Neither document constrains the other and the combination has not been substantiated.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a minimum separation between a repair boundary and a termination to both documents.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the plate and fitting part numbers that the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The bonding resistance acceptance does not distinguish a repaired panel from an intact one. If a repaired termination is permitted at all it needs either the same limit stated explicitly or its own.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a note that a repaired panel is measured against the same limit with no allowance.

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the modification to its retrofit bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin accomplishment instructions send the technician to the repair task where a fastener hole is outside limits, but say nothing about a panel that already carries a scarf repair, which is the case that actually arose.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a pre-embodiment check for an existing repair to the bulletin.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The two schemes are compatible subject to a stated separation, which three documents must now carry.
